$comment: Exceptions for scripts/check-prod-audit.mjs. Every Critical/High advisory in `pnpm audit --prod`
must appear here or CI fails. Entries expire; an expired entry fails the same gate. An entry whose
advisory no longer appears also fails, so the list cannot only grow and cannot silently pre-approve
a re-introduction. Removing an entry is the fix in that case.
This list is the state on 2026-08-11, not an endorsement of it. #328 owns clearing it.

2026-08-12: the eight nuxt-closure reasons said core-app's vue-sonner optional peer. Measured wrong — moving vue-sonner to devDependencies changed the --prod audit by zero advisories. The real path is apps/nexus's @sentry/nuxt. An exception list is only worth its reasons.
2026-08-12: `module`, `severity` and `versions` are now checked against what the audit actually

Reaches --prod only through listhen@1.10.0, the local HTTP(S) listener behind `nuxt dev` / `nitro dev` (it also mints the self-signed dev certificate). Traced with `pnpm why node-forge --prod`: listhen -> @nuxt/cli@3.37.0 -> nuxt, and listhen -> nitropack@2.13.4 -> @talex-touch/tuff-nexus. Not in the deployed worker: no file under nitropack/dist/runtime imports listhen; only dist/core/index.mjs and dist/cli/dev.mjs do. The advisory is RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepting extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements, and no runtime path verifies a signature with node-forge. No patched release exists (vulnerable <= 1.4.0, first_patched_version null). Remove this entry and upgrade when node-forge ships a fix.

The runtime the packaged app ships. Reaches --prod through the root package.json's electron ^41.10.6 dependency and through @electron-toolkit/preload and @electron-toolkit/utils, production dependencies of @talex-touch/core-app that take electron as a peer (`pnpm audit --prod --json`, 3 paths). The advisory is Chromium's distrust of compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates: until the runtime moves, the app's network stack still accepts certificates chained to them. No 41.x release carries the fix (patched in 42.11.16, 43.8.1, 44.9.1 and 45.0.0-beta.6), and leaving Electron 41 is a major upgrade with its own native-module and packaging verification. Remove this entry when core-app moves to a patched major.

LangChain 0.3's own copy. Reaches --prod only through @langchain/core@0.3.80 and @langchain/langgraph@0.4.9 (zod ^3.25.32) and @langchain/openai@0.4.9 (zod ^3.22.4), with @langchain/anthropic reaching it through @langchain/core; production dependencies of apps/core-app, apps/nexus and packages/tuff-intelligence (`pnpm audit --prod --json`, 34 paths). LangChain validates tool arguments and structured output with it, so an oversized collection would have to come from the configured model provider's response, in core-app's main process, packages/tuff-intelligence or Nexus's server/utils/tuffIntelligenceLangChainProviderAdapters.ts. The advisory is memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections. No 3.x release is patched (vulnerable < 4.6.6); the zod 4 copy moved to 4.6.6 in the same change. Remove this entry when LangChain moves to a release that runs on zod 4.
